text: On Searle's distinction between original and derived intentionality, the word 'cat' printed on a page:
choices: Has original, intrinsic intentionality, since it directly refers to cats
Has no intentionality of any kind
Has derived intentionality — it is about cats only because language users mean cats by it
Has exactly the same kind of intentionality as a thought about cats
explanation: For Searle, marks and symbols have only derived intentionality: they are 'about' things because minds with original (intrinsic) intentionality interpret them so. A thought about cats, by contrast, has original intentionality. Option 0 conflates the two; option 1 overstates matters (the word does have aboutness, just derived); option 3 denies the very distinction Searle draws.
